calibration_source: Eurostat (namq_10_gdp, namq_10_pe, namq_10_a10_e, demo_pjanbroad, lfsi_emp_a, irt_st_m), OECD LFS, Riksbank

x_comments.alpha_K: Capital share set to 0.33 for cross-country comparability with Germany, Poland and Spain, all of which use 0.33 in the Ramsey layer. Holding alpha_K fixed across countries keeps the Ramsey trends comparable.
x_comments.delta_annual: 5.5% annual depreciation for total-economy capital, between Germany/Spain (5%) and Poland (6%). Sweden is a mature economy like Germany, but its capital stock carries an unusually high ICT and R&D share, and those assets depreciate far faster than structures. PWT composite rates for Sweden sit around 5.5-6%. This is the one Swedish structural input with no sharp empirical pin in this repo; if the Ramsey K/Y comes out far from the PIM value, revisit it first.
x_comments.beta_annual: Discount factor: 0.96 annual, as for the other three countries. It pins the terminal modified-golden-rule BGP real rate jointly with sigma and tfp_growth_annual; the resulting r* is written to documentation_data/ramsey/ramsey_summary_Sweden.json (structural.r_star_annual) rather than quoted here, because it is derived and would go stale.
x_comments.sigma: Inverse IES (CRRA coefficient). sigma=1.5 is mid-range consensus (1=log, 2=high risk aversion), same as the other three.
x_comments.tfp_growth_annual: 0.65% annual labour-augmenting TFP growth, DERIVED FROM THIS SAMPLE rather than assumed. Over 2001q1-2025q1 the Swedish levels data give GDP per hour growth of 0.98% p.a.; on a BGP where K grows with Y, g_A = g_(Y/L) * (1 - alpha_K) = 0.98% * 0.67 = 0.65%. This is the HIGHEST of the four implemented countries (Germany 0.5%, Spain 0.4%, Poland 1.5% in-sample but converging to 0.5%), which matches Sweden's comparatively strong measured productivity performance over the period.
x_comments.phi: Inverse Frisch elasticity on extensive margin. PROVISIONAL: set to 1.3 (the German value, calibrated there from a SimPaths wage-shift response surface). No Swedish SimPaths experiments exist yet, so this carries no Sweden-specific information and should be re-estimated from dedicated Swedish SimPaths runs when available. Same status as Spain's 1.3 and Poland's 1.35.
x_comments.labor_supply: Default Ramsey labor-supply mode. calibrate_growth_model.m copies this template into simpaths_export and writes the calibrated runtime fields there.

base_year_values.WAP_comment: Working-age population (15-64), thousands. Source: Eurostat demo_pjanbroad (A.NR.Y15-64.T.SE), Sweden 2001 = 5,721,081 persons. Must match build_population_projection.m age range.
base_year_values.x_comment: calibrate_growth_model.m writes calibrated base-year levels and derived fields into simpaths_export/Sweden/growth_params_Sweden.json.

inflation_target.x_comment: Riksbank 2% target. Numerically the same as the ECB's, but it is an INDEPENDENT national target, in force since 1993 and restated on the CPIF measure in 2017 - not an imported one as for Spain. The whole 2001q1 sample sits inside that regime. pi_star entered as annual percent.

labor_trends.nawru_source: PLACEHOLDER: HP trend (lambda=160000) of the in-sample ILO unemployment rate, written by calibrate_growth_model.m. Intended source: AMECO.
labor_trends.demographic_L_source: PLACEHOLDER: HP trend (lambda=160000) of the in-sample labour force, written by calibrate_growth_model.m; no projection tail. Intended source: Eurostat population projections + SCB (Statistics Sweden) labor force participation.
labor_trends.x_comment: nawru_file is read for diagnostics only. demographic_L_file has no post-sample tail, so ramsey_trend.m extends N at its trailing 20-quarter trend growth rate, untapered, until build_population_projection.m supplies a projection. Hours: log-linear trend fitted to observed.

solver.x_comment: Stacked-time Newton (LBJ) perfect-foresight solver with terminal K/Y closure. 400 terminal quarters (~100 years) as for Germany and Spain; Poland needs 600 only because its terminal_growth block has to converge a catch-up TFP path, which Sweden does not have. Newton convergence requires ||F||_inf <= 1.0e-10 within 200 iterations.
